title: Canonical derived section pairing from adapted resolutions and its coherence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to its module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $W$ an object and $A=\mathcal O(W)$. Let $E(M)=M(W)$ on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] be exact and preserve all small colimits. Assume the actual section pairings $E(M)\otimes_AE(N)\to E(M\otimes_{\mathcal O}N)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with unit $A\to E(\mathcal O)$ the identity, are isomorphisms satisfying the ordinary symmetric monoidal diagrams. Assume every unbounded complex $K$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with flat terms, with both $P$ and $E(P)$ K-flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Write $G=D(E)$ for termwise localization on the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The section pairings induce a canonical natural transformation
$$c_{K,L}:G(K)\otimes_A^L G(L)\longrightarrow G(K\otimes_{\mathcal O}^L L).$$
It is normalized on every pair of flat-term K-flat complexes $P,Q$ by the composite from the derived tensor of $E(P),E(Q)$ to their ordinary total tensor (the canonical derived-to-ordinary comparison), then the section pairing into $E(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q))$, and the canonical sheaf K-flat model comparison. This specifies the comparison independently of all resolutions, natural for arbitrary derived morphisms, not just chain maps. For every pair of complexes the ordinary total section pairing is a chain isomorphism, with degree $n$ component
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p(W)\otimes_AQ^q(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}(\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q^q)(W),$$
commuting with $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. On adapted resolutions as above both evaluated complexes are K-flat, so $c_{K,L}$ is an isomorphism. With the prescribed derived constraints [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], these maps and $A[0]\to G(\mathcal O[0])=A[0]$ satisfy associativity, symmetry and both unit diagrams. On representatives the diagrams are respectively unsigned reassociation of $(p,q,r)$, $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$, and scalar multiplication; localization preserves their equalities. No claim that $E$ preserves every K-flat complex is assumed.

proof.text: Write $t$ for direct-sum total tensor and $b_{P,Q}:t(E(P),E(Q))\to E(t(P,Q))$ for the ordinary total section map. In degree $n$ take the direct sum of the assumed section isomorphisms in bidegrees $p+q=n$, followed by the coproduct comparison for $E$. Both maps are isomorphisms by the hypotheses. Naturality of the section pairing with respect to $d_P$ and $d_Q$, and additivity of evaluation, give $b(d_Px\otimes y+(-1)^px\otimes d_Qy)=E(d)(b(x\otimes y))$. Thus $b$ is the asserted chain isomorphism for arbitrary complexes, natural for cochain maps. This calculation uses no flatness or boundedness.

proof.text: Let $Q_{\mathcal O}$ and $Q_A$ denote cochain localizations; view $A$-modules as module sheaves on the one-object point site. Exactness of $E$ identifies $H^n(E(K))$ with $E(H^nK)$, since $E$ preserves kernels, images and their quotients. Hence it preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and the localization universal property gives $G$ and its termwise factorization $GQ_{\mathcal O}\cong Q_AE$. Let $\mathcal P$ be the full cochain subcategory of flat-term K-flat sheaf complexes. Its two-variable restriction is fully faithful on functor categories by the cochain model rigidity theorem. No assertion about $E(\mathcal P)$ being K-flat is made here.

proof.text:
Use the canonical lax tensorator $m^A_{U,V}:Q_AU\otimes_A^LQ_AV\to Q_At(U,V)$ of native localization; it is natural for all complexes, and invertible when either input is K-flat. On $P,Q\in\mathcal P$ define a transformation from $(K,L)\mapsto GK\otimes_A^LGL$ to $(K,L)\mapsto G(K\otimes_{\mathcal O}^LL)$ by
$$m^A_{E(P),E(Q)}\ ;\ Q_A(b_{P,Q})\ ;\ G(r_{P,Q}),$$
with the termwise factorization inserted, where $r_{P,Q}:Q_{\mathcal O}t(P,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal O}P\otimes_{\mathcal O}^LQ_{\mathcal O}Q$ is the fixed K-flat model comparison. All three factors are natural on this cochain subcategory. Fullness in Step 2 extends this transformation to $c$ on derived categories, and faithfulness gives uniqueness. In particular this is the prescribed normalization on every flat-term K-flat pair, including pairs whose evaluations are not known to be K-flat. Naturality for arbitrary derived arrows is part of this extension, rather than an assertion only for chain maps.

proof.text: For any $K,L$, choose the adapted quasi-isomorphisms $P\to K$, $Q\to L$ in the hypotheses. Then $P,Q\in\mathcal P$ and $E(P),E(Q)$ are K-flat. The first factor of Step 3 is invertible by the native localization theorem, the second by Step 1, and the third is a functor applied to an isomorphism. Therefore $c_{Q_{\mathcal O}P,Q_{\mathcal O}Q}$ is invertible. Naturality along the two localized resolution isomorphisms conjugates this component to $c_{K,L}$, so every component is invertible. Two choices of resolutions give this same already defined natural transformation by the uniqueness in Step 3. Only the selected adapted resolutions are used for this invertibility argument.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction); Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); ordinary section calculation in Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Lemma 4.1(1)

proof.text: Check associativity on $P,Q,R\in\mathcal P$. Their two total tensors are again flat-term K-flat representatives by the total-tensor model lemma, so Step 3 computes the inner and outer comparisons in both routes. Cancel the source K-flat model comparisons using compatibility of native localization with associators. The lax associativity equation for $m^A$ reduces the two routes to localization of the ordinary $b$ associativity square. On each summand $(p,q,r)$ that square is the assumed ordinary section-pairing associativity square, with unsigned reassociation $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$. Coproduct universality gives equality of chain maps. The differential is $d_P+(-1)^pd_Q+(-1)^{p+q}d_R$ in both parenthesizations. Thus the derived associativity equation holds on these triples. Every derived object is isomorphic to a localized representative in $\mathcal P$; naturality conjugates the equation to arbitrary triples. These are precisely the prescribed derived associators of the closed symmetric monoidal theorem.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction); Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); ordinary section calculation in Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Lemma 4.1(1)

proof.text: For symmetry, on bidegree $(p,q)$ both routes through the ordinary $b$ square apply the assumed ordinary sheaf symmetry and multiply by $(-1)^{pq}$. Evaluation preserves this integer scalar; hence the square commutes. The native localization braiding compatibility and the prescribed derived Koszul symmetry identify its localization with the braided equation for $c$. For the left and right unit diagrams use $\mathcal O[0]$, a flat-term K-flat complex since tensoring with it is the identity, and $E(\mathcal O[0])=A[0]$. The ordinary diagrams both send $a\otimes x$ or $x\otimes a$ to $ax$, by the assumed section unit and its ordinary coherence. The localization unit comparison is invertible and compatible with both unitors, so Step 3 gives the same two derived unit equations with unit map the identity $A[0]\to G(\mathcal O[0])$. As in Step 5, conjugation by representative isomorphisms extends these equations to all inputs. Together with Step 4 these equations make $G$ strong symmetric monoidal.
